<hr>

I have had to revise what I'm waiting for and have been temporarily banishing, or at least redistributing, ennui in hospital by looking at the Introduction and Overview to a forthcoming book of essays on predicativism edited by Laura Crosilla,  Øystein Linnebo, and Michael Rathjen. [It is freely available here.](https://academic.oup.com/book/63460/chapter/577772313)

Laura Crosilla contributes two sections. She first sketches Weyl's evolving and varying ideas on the foundations of mathematics, though his predicativism will be the focus of this book. Then she has a section on Predicativity Beyond Weyl.

The remaining long section gives thumbnail sketches of the sixteen contributions in the book, with indications of many intriguing papers for anyone with a prior interest in predicativism. This looks a very worthwhile collection.

(Those relatively new to predicativism, or sceptical about its current significance, might want to see if their interest is piqued by two *SEP* pieces: [the elementary §2.4 in the general entry on the Philosophy of Mathematics](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/philosophy-mathematics/) And then for the setting for modern concerns with predicativism see the entry on [Reverse Mathematics](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/reverse-mathematics/))
